summary: A first-person reflection on a series of mental health wellness workshops at a local community center, led by psychologist Dr. Emily Rutherford and life coach Marcus Li. Sessions covered myths about mental health, emotional intelligence, resilience and coping toolkits, nutrition, and mindful yoga, with guest instructors. The author describes growing awareness, community and empowerment, and a commitment to keep nurturing mental well-being independently.
one_line: The author reflects on a month of community wellness workshops on mental health, emotional intelligence, resilience, nutrition, yoga and community support.
key_facts: The reflection is dated September 5, 2023, though it describes sessions running through October 10th.
The workshops were led by psychologist Dr. Emily Rutherford and facilitated by life coach Marcus Li, and were held at a local community center on Saturday mornings.
Marcus Li explained that mental health is a spectrum about mental well-being, like physical fitness, and can fluctuate.

The September 19th session focused on emotional intelligence and self-awareness, using guided meditation and journaling; Dr. Rutherford presented emotional intelligence as a skill that can be developed.
The September 26th session focused on resilience and coping strategies such as mindfulness, exercise, creative outlets and social support.
Dr. Rutherford compared a personalized mental health toolkit to items needed when climbing a mountain.
Marcus Li shared his own journey, saying that building a robust support system was crucial to his well-being.
Nutritionist Chloe Kim spoke on October 3rd about the link between diet and mental wellness, covering omega-3 fatty acids, antioxidants and gut health.
Yoga instructor Alex Torres led a mindful movement yoga class on October 10th, saying "Yoga is not about touching your toes; it's about what you learn on the way down."
In the penultimate session, participants reported lowered anxiety, improved relationships, and breakthroughs in lifelong struggles.
The author says the workshops left them with a sense of empowerment and responsibility to keep nurturing mental well-being.
